title: camera_set_fit has zero callers after the resting-call-site migration, yet its comment claims it 'is the explicit OUT LIMIT'
detail: Dead proc retained: all four resting call sites now route to camera_set_default, and the actual out-limit is the CAM_ZOOM_MIN clamp in effect_zoom (main.odin:1991). The present-tense comment describes a role the code no longer plays.
recommended_fix: Delete camera_set_fit (recoverable from git history if a whole-map-jump action is ever wanted), or rewrite its comment to past tense with no 'OUT LIMIT' framing.

title: The tier ladder's 'non-overlapping by construction' claim is unenforced: focus tiers 2.3/2.6 are unnamed literals and the ladder test pins its own literals
evidence: camera.odin:47 claims 'The three tiers are non-overlapping by construction:' but main.odin:1778 'app.cam_zoom_to = 2.3', main.odin:1794/1819 'app.cam_zoom_to = 2.6' are inline magic numbers, and the guard test restates its own literals rather than reading them: camera_test.odin:138-139 'testing.expect(t, DEFAULT_ZOOM < 2.3, "the node focus (2.3) is an extra zoom-in above the default")' / 'testing.expect(t, 2.3 < 2.6, ...)'. No test anywhere pins camera_set_selection's/camera_focus_pair's zoom targets (grep for 'cam_zoom_to == 2.' in tests: none).
detail: Editing 2.3 to 1.9 in camera_set_selection inverts the ladder (focus below the 2.0 default) and fails zero tests — the new tier model's core invariant is guarded only by constants that don't reference the real values.
recommended_fix: Hoist FOCUS_ZOOM_NODE :: 2.3 and FOCUS_ZOOM_LINK :: 2.6 into camera.odin beside DEFAULT_ZOOM/CAM_ZOOM_MIN; make camera_set_selection, camera_focus_pair, and camera_default_zoom_is_the_resting_tier read the named constants.

title: Auto-pullback is silently disabled for any camera below DEFAULT_ZOOM — an undocumented dead band the function comment does not state
detail: The a11y auto-pullback (default ON) never fires while the player holds a manual zoom below 2.0, even for districts outside that viewport — emergent from reusing DEFAULT_ZOOM as the floor; consistent with the directive's spirit but undocumented.
recommended_fix: Add one sentence to camera_pullback_target's doc: 'any camera already below DEFAULT_ZOOM disables the pullback entirely (the player owns the wide view)'.

title: PR body claims 'palcheck floors re-pinned where the puck shrink dropped pixel counts' — no palcheck change exists in the diff and the commit message states the opposite
evidence: PR body: '- **palcheck floors re-pinned where the puck shrink dropped pixel counts** (e.g. the puck hardware-tone floor) — measured on the re-blessed frames, keeping the crop/blit-canary job (a missing sprite still zeroes the count).' But git show 9bf9797 --stat lists only _pr_body_camera_zoom_tiers.md, app/main.odin, app/pullback_test.odin, app/render/{camera,camera_test,dublin,sprites}.odin + goldens — harness/palcheck.odin is untouched (hardware-tone floor still '> 200'), and the commit message says: 'palcheck stays green (floors had margin) - no re-pin needed.'
detail: The declared spec (PR body IS the spec) contains a false verify-claim about the golden re-bless discipline; the actual state is fine, but the spec text misleads review and future re-pin archaeology.
recommended_fix: Correct the PR body line to match reality: 'palcheck stays green — floors had margin under the puck shrink, no re-pin needed.'

title: camera_cluster_center computes the whole-topology centroid; its 'source cluster' contract holds only at the single call instant after fixture seeding
evidence: // camera_cluster_center — the centroid of the live nodes (world px): the 'source terminal / first cluster' home anchor (v2-camera-zoom-tiers). The app calls it immediately after seeding the fixture (start_run) — at that instant the topology holds EXACTLY the fixture's nodes, so the centroid IS the first cluster. The body walks every live node (for i in 0..<len(topo.node_alive) { ... ax/f32(n) }) with no cluster scoping.
detail: A pure function whose name promises cluster semantics but whose math is an all-nodes centroid; any future caller (or a start_run reordering that moves the call past growth spawns) silently gets a whole-map centroid as the 'home'.
recommended_fix: Rename to camera_topology_centroid (comment keeps the seeding-instant contract), or accept the fixture node ids explicitly so the anchor cannot drift with call timing.
